item.title: Database Changes Lost During .NET Debugging Persistent Data Issues Explained
item.description:
“Database Changes Lost During .NET Debugging Persistent Data Issues Explained”

When developing applications that interact with databases, particularly within a .NET development environment like Visual Studio, a common frustration arises: changes made to the database during a debug session disappear upon restarting the application or inspecting the database through tools like Visual Studio’s Server Explorer. This behavior stems from how Visual Studio manages project files and their output.

The core of the issue often lies with the |DataDirectory| substitution string in your connection string and the “Copy to Output Directory” property of your database file.

item.title: Debug vs Release Builds: Why Local Variables Behave Differently in .NET
item.description:
“Debug vs Release Builds: Why Local Variables Behave Differently in .NET”

Have you ever encountered a scenario in .NET development where your code behaves perfectly in a Debug build but exhibits peculiar results when switched to Release? A common culprit is the differing treatment of local variables by the Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler, especially when debugging tools are involved. This can lead to seemingly contradictory outcomes related to object lifetimes and garbage collection.
